title: [finding] metadata: database-loader spells its own driver-capability predicate inline, duplicating resolveDriverExec one directory away
body:
Found while implementing #14083, which aligned the three raw-SQL resolvers in `packages/metadata-protocol` to `execute`-first. This is a fourth site that carries the same *predicate* but is deliberately **not** part of that card, and it is recorded rather than folded in.

## The site

`packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts`, line 403, inside the engine branch of the schema-ready path:

```ts
if (c && (typeof c.raw === 'function' || typeof c.execute === 'function')) {
  driver = candidate as IDataDriver;
  break;
}
```

## Why this is NOT the #14083 defect

⛔ It is not an order divergence, and #14083 was right to leave it alone. The check is an `OR` used to pick which candidate out of `engineAny.drivers` is raw-SQL-capable; it selects a **driver**, never a **surface**. The surface decision happens one call later, inside `migrateProjectIdToEnvironmentId(driver)`, which already routes through `packages/metadata/src/migrations/driver-exec.ts` (`resolveDriverExec`, `execute`-first). Swapping the two operands here changes nothing.

## What is worth recording

The predicate is spelled inline, a third time, in the same package that already owns the canonical answer. `resolveDriverExec` **is** the definition of "this driver can run raw SQL" — `resolveDriverExec(d) !== undefined` — and `driver-exec.ts` is one directory away from this file. Two consequences, both small today:

- The two can drift. If the resolution ever grows a third surface, or tightens what counts (for example rejecting a non-callable member of the right name), this predicate keeps answering the old question and silently selects a driver the resolver will then refuse.
- It is the last remaining inline copy in `packages/metadata`. #14083 collapsed the three copies in `metadata-protocol` into one helper and defined that package's predicate as the resolution succeeding, precisely so the two cannot disagree; the same move is available here and is a one-line change.

⚠️ Deliberately not claiming a live defect: the current operands are exactly the two surfaces `resolveDriverExec` tries, so the predicate and the resolution agree today. This is a drift-risk observation, not a measured misbehaviour.

## Known limitation this inherits, unchanged

`typeof driver.execute === 'function'` cannot separate "declares the surface" from "can actually run SQL" — two shipped drivers satisfy the non-optional declaration and execute nothing. That is #14082's subject, is unaffected by anything above, and would be the thing to fix first if this predicate is ever revisited.

## Re-run

```sh
sed -n '395,410p' packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts
git grep -n "resolveDriverExec" -- packages/metadata/src
```

Whole-tree sweep for the dual-surface shape, which is how this was found:

```sh
for f in $(git grep -lE "typeof [A-Za-z_.()]*\braw\b[^=]*=== ?'function'" -- packages apps examples); do
  grep -qE "typeof [A-Za-z_.()]*\bexecute\b[^=]*=== ?'function'" "$f" && echo "$f"
done
```

⚠️ That sweep needs a firing pathspec. The `packages/*/src` form used in #14083's original re-run block matches **zero** files under git's pathspec rules, so it reports a clean zero whatever the tree contains; the positive control is the same regex for `execute`, which finds 327 member definitions under `packages`.

At the time of writing the dual-surface sweep returns exactly three files: this one, `packages/metadata/src/migrations/driver-exec.ts` and `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/driver-exec.ts` (the two canonical helpers). The five other `raw` probes in the tree are local variables named `raw` on HTTP headers and request objects, not driver surfaces.

## Dedup declaration

Repo-scoped REST listing of all 282 open issues, bodies included, grepped locally for `database-loader`, `resolveDriverExec`, `driverCanRunSql`, `driver-exec` and `capability predicate`. Only `database-loader` matched, returning #14037 and #14038 — both members of the #13973 driver-`Date`-materialisation census, neither about driver-capability probing. Control: the same fetched list grepped for `metadata-protocol` returned 16 issues, so the channel was answering. No duplicate found.

Backlink: #14083, where the sibling package's three copies were collapsed.
